knowledge_point.title: Converting a Radical to a Unit Fraction Exponent

question.:question/worked-solution:
The radical $\sqrt[n]{x}$ can be written using a fractional exponent as ${x}^{1/n}.$

Comparing $\sqrt[n]{x}$ with $\sqrt[5]{2},$ we get $x=2,$ and $n=5.$ Therefore,

$$
\sqrt[5]{2}={2}^{1/5}
$$

generation.domain: indexed x=2..15,n=3..10,x!=n,(x,n)!=(2,4); square n=2,x=2..15 or declared positive decimals, neighboring eligible bases
